newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Mexico petrochemical sell-off was minor - Zedillo.
newsitem.headline: Mexico petrochemical sell-off was minor - Zedillo.

text.p: Mexico's plans to privatise its petrochemical industry -- which were recently scrapped after intense political and union opposition -- were a minor part of the privatisation programme as a whole, Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo said on Thursday.

Zedillo, in Singapore for an official visit, was responding to a question from a reporter at a breakfast meeting with the press. The reporter asked if Mexico's structural reform programme was piecemeal and cited the recent climbdown over petrochemical privatisation as an example.
"I fully disagree with you. I think you have the wrong information," Zedillo said.
"The petrochemical privatisation plan was a very minor proportion of the whole privatisation programme," he said.
"Our privatisation programme has already been successful," Zedillo said, adding that Mexico was the leader of the privatisation process in Latin America, well before Argentina and Brazil.
He cited privatisation programmes in the banking, steel and sugar mill sectors as examples of this.
The government's four-year struggle to privatise the petrochemical industry was formally scrapped last month. -- Singapore Newsroom (+65 870 3080)
